newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says IMF programme still on track.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says IMF programme still on track.

text.p: Pakistan said on Sunday its agreement with the IMF was still on track and a mission from the fund would visit soon to review economic performance.

"The performance of the economy has been well within the targets established with the IMF in December and therefore the programme supported by IMF resources under SBA (standby arrangement) remains on track," the Finance Ministry said.
It said in a statement that an IMF mission would arrive in the next few weeks to review economic performance up to December and to be briefed on developments in January and February.

It said Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif had met Abbas Mirakhor, who represents Pakistan on the IMF's executive board, in Lahore on Sunday in the presence of Sartaj Aziz and Ishaq Dar, both tipped to get economic ministries in Sharif's cabinet.
"Mr Mirakhor was briefed on the economic priorities of the new government and on their programme for the revitalisation of production and productivity in Pakistan," it said.
Mirakhor agreed to pass on a request from Sharif for IMF assistance in strengthening tax administration in Pakistan.

The IMF resumed and expanded a standby loan to Pakistan in December after the caretaker government promised to cut the budget deficit to four percent of gross domestic product in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) from 6.3 percent in 1995/96.
The IMF has been anxious to know whether Sharif, who returned to power after a landslide election victory on February 3, is fully committed to the targets agreed with the fund.
Sharif and Aziz have both cast doubt on whether the four percent deficit target can be met in the current fiscal year.
Sharif, who has yet to name his cabinet, was due to address the nation later on Sunday to outline his priorities.
